recommendation: Keep the source fix. It preserves the approved pattern-example approach while removing misleading baseDefinition guidance from the active StructureDefinition explanatory section; no separate clinical artifact was added because current source already has active pattern/logical-model examples and the remaining issue was stale example text.
issue_request: FHIR-28306 was Published/Persuasive for R5. It reported that logical-model examples were missing and that StructureDefinition explanatory text did not make type and baseDefinition usage clear; the Jira resolution called for pointing to existing pattern examples and adding a clinical example.
initial_application: No local commit message explicitly mentioned FHIR-28306. Untagged commit cddf6ad4580b2b6d0ee53927f8c86ab585ce9bcb added a logical-model example to source/structuredefinition/structuredefinition-notes.xml and is contained in v5.0.0; later FHIR-37543 work restored and linked the current Logical Models page.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes for 2020-12-07 record FHIR-28306 as 'Will point to existing pattern examples' at 11-0-0. Current source has an active logical.html page and pattern cross-reference, but StructureDefinition notes still used stale 'base' wording and invalid hl7.org/fhir/us/core Base/DomainResource canonicals in examples. Zulip discussion around logical model instances confirms the colorectal example context and implementer confusion about logical model base classes.
reconciliation: Changed source/structuredefinition/structuredefinition-notes.xml to refer to baseDefinition and to use core FHIR Base/DomainResource canonicals for the Resource, CanonicalResource, and logical Definition examples.
source_changes: source/structuredefinition/structuredefinition-notes.xml: corrected example baseDefinition URLs from hl7.org/fhir/us/core to core FHIR StructureDefinition canonicals for Base and DomainResource.

related_jiras.note: Restored the Logical Models page and pattern cross-reference; already represented on the combined branch and used as context only.
